candidate.answerReason: A is one day after C. Equal sums therefore require the unknown date to be one day after B, which is the date behind P.

methods.label: Compare the dates in each sum
methods.explanation:
Dates increase by one when moving one box to the right within a calendar row. Thus \(A\) is one day after \(C\).

[Figure 1](figures/1990_AMC_8_Q10_question_fig1.svg)

Let \(c\) and \(b\) be the dates behind \(C\) and \(B\), and let \(x\) be the required date. The date behind \(A\) is \(c+1\), so the equal-sum condition becomes
\[
x+c=(c+1)+b.
\]
Subtracting \(c\) from both sides gives \(x=b+1\). We therefore need the date immediately after \(B\). The calendar places \(P\) immediately to the right of \(B\), so the letter is \(\boxed{P}\), choice \(\text{A}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses consecutive calendar dates and subtraction of a common addend from a simple equality.
